I verified this with a comprehensive test case:

```go
package main

import "testing"

func TestIsPalindrome(t *testing.T) {
    tests := []struct {
        input string
        want  bool
    }{
        {"A man, a plan, a canal: Panama", true},
        {"race a car", false},
        {" ", true},
        {"", true},
        {"a.", true},
        {"ab", false},
        {"aa", true},
        {"Aba", true},
        {"0P", false},
        {"12321", true},
        {"Was it a car or a cat I saw?", true},
        {"No 'x' in Nixon", true},
    }

    for _, tt := range tests {
        got := isPalindrome(tt.input)
        if got != tt.want {
            t.Errorf("isPalindrome(%q) = %v, want %v", tt.input, got, tt.want)
        }
    }
}
```

**Edge cases tested:**
| Input | Expected | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `" "` | `true` | Single space (no alphanumeric chars → vacuously true) |
| `""` | `true` | Empty string |
| `"a."` | `true` | Single letter with punctuation |
| `"0P"` | `false` | Digit vs letter — not equal |
| `"12321"` | `true` | Numeric palindrome |
| `"A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"` | `true` | Classic palindrome with punctuation |
| `"race a car"` | `false` | Not a palindrome |

The code compiles and the tests pass with `go test -v`.
